title: Scalar change and pullback commute on ordered finite Tate lines
statement:
Let $R,A$ be finite commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to A$ a unital ring homomorphism, and $N\ge1$ with $NR=NA=0$. Let $u:X'\to X$ be a scheme morphism with $N$ invertible in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Write $L_{D,X}(d)=D_X(d)[2d]$ for the ordered etale Tate tensor and $T_{D,X}(d)=\nu_X^*L_{D,X}(d)$ for its canonical ordinary pro-etale derived comparison [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows, def-amb-vector-integration]. Supply normalized ordinary root and line pullback data for $D=R,A$ [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows] and normalized coefficient-line comparisons $s_X,s_{X'}$ at the common exponent $N$ [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows]. Let $P_D=u_D^*$, $S_V=(-)\otimes_R^LA$ on the scheme $V$, and let $\lambda:P_AS_X\simeq S_{X'}P_R$ be the canonical comparison [def-sp-proetale-scalar-pullback-iso]. Let $\tau_D:P_DT_{D,X}(d)\to T_{D,X'}(d)$ be site comparison followed by the normalized root/tensor/shift pullback, and let $\sigma_V:S_VT_{R,V}(d)\to T_{A,V}(d)$ be $\mathrm{proTwistMap}(d,s_V)$. Then for every $d\in\mathbf N$, writing composition right to left,
$$\tau_A\circ P_A(\sigma_X)=\sigma_{X'}\circ S_{X'}(\tau_R)\circ\lambda_{T_{R,X}(d)}.$$
This involves only Tate lines and the specified comparisons; no dualizing object, orientation or exceptional functor is assumed.

proof.text: At the common positive exponent N, roots_power and monicity of the kernel inclusion force each scalar root map to be the identity. The two normalized root pullbacks therefore commute with them. Their line maps agree on all root/coefficient generators. The balanced finite Tate comparison gives the ordinary and derived unit and first-root squares; these canonical comparisons agree with the supplied normalized comparisons by their generator equations.

Induct on the ordered tensor power d. At zero use the constant-unit square. At a successor apply the tensor scalar/pullback coherence to the preceding line and the root line shifted by two. Bounded flat complexes compute the derived tensor, and the integer-shift comparisons preserve its normalization. The root order is unchanged and all shifts are even.
Apply site comparison and use the canonical etale/pro-etale scalar/pullback cube. Its two composites are exactly the displayed proTwistMap and Tate pullback routes.

lean.statement:
theorem tate_scalar_pullback_coherence
    {R A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Finite R] [Finite A]
    (φ : R →+* A) (N : ℕ) (_hN : 0 < N) (hR : (N : R) = 0) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (twR : Etale.OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport R N hR)
    (twA : Etale.OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (u' : X' ⟶ X) (hX : IsUnit (N : Γ(X, ⊤))) (d : ℕ)
    (sX : CoefficientLineComparison φ N N hR hA X)
    (sX' : CoefficientLineComparison φ N N hR hA X') :
    (proPullback A u').map (proTwistMap d sX) ≫
        ((sitePullbackIso A u').app (line A N hA X d) ≪≫
          (comparison A X').mapIso
            (Etale.vectorIntegrationBaseCoefficientPullback A N hA twA u' hX d)).hom =
      (scalarPullbackProEtaleIso φ u').hom.app ((comparison R X).obj (line R N hR X d)) ≫
        (proScalar φ X').map
          ((sitePullbackIso R u').app (line R N hR X d) ≪≫
            (comparison R X').mapIso
              (Etale.vectorIntegrationBaseCoefficientPullback R N hR twR u' hX d)).hom ≫
          proTwistMap d sX'
